notes: Both italic 'look' tokens left added under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause: the clauses are verbless with an אֶל predicate, and 'look' names an act of the eyes rather than a bare copula, on the terms of 'My soul waiteth for the Lord'. Competing reading puts each as the construction copula on the אֶל (rule 49); the ASV italic corroborates the supply without deciding it (rule 7).

Large-unit check: עַד + שֶׁ → 'Until' retained as one fused unit. The single English word carries both the limit sense of עַד and the subordinating force of שֶׁ, and no second English word is spent on either, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met; headed on עַד as the governing morpheme standing first (rule 23).
'upon' of 'have mercy upon us' stays with the light-verb rendering of יְּחָנֵּ (rule 44, suffix-object clause), the suffix keeping only 'us' (rule 18).
